body_markdown:
Mecum’s Monterey auction topped $100M this year, largely thanks to massive results for modern exotics. In fact, eight of Mecum’s 10 most expensive lots at Monterey 2026 were European supercars built after 1990. But aside from a few huge sales at the top, this was a typical Mecum Monterey auction, as reflected by the $66,000 median price. Numerous Monterey auctions have come and gone over the years that cater to lower budgets in addition to the private jet crowd, but Mecum is the last one left with a heaping helping of sub-$100K classics.


We were on the ground in Monterey and looked over the most important cars crossing the block over the course of the week. Here, we examine some of the favorites from Mecum.


## Lot S24.1: 1972 Datsun 240Z


Mecum


**Sold for $93,500**


*Chassis no. HLS3054807. Blue Metallic over white vinyl. Unrestored original, #2+ condition.*


**Equipment:** 2.4-L/151-hp I-6, five-speed, wheel covers, custom exhaust, aftermarket sway bars, heater, AM/FM radio.


**Condition:** Sold new in Oregon. Showing 9607 miles that are represented as actual. Fitted with a five-speed from a later Z-car, but the original four-speed is included. This is a remarkably well-preserved Datsun with few clues that it’s a 54-year-old sports car. It’s not completely stock, but the mods are things you can’t see, are reversible, and improve the experience behind the wheel.


**Bottom line:** The original 240Z’s main appeal as a new car in the early ’70s was value combined with reliability. It was quicker and more practical than many of the finicky European sports cars it competed against, while carrying a much more attractive sticker price. So big was the original Z-car’s impact on the Japanese car market in the U.S. and performance cars in general that, ironically, it’s become quite collectible. Long gone are the days when a clean 240Z was an entry-level classic. Perfect ones can crack $100K, and this one almost got there. It sold on Bring a Trailer in January of this year for[$79,800](https://bringatrailer.com/listing/1972-datsun-240z-382/) , but found an even more receptive audience in Monterey.


## Lot F107: 2009 Ferrari 430 Scuderia Spider 16M


Mecum


**Sold for $1,001,000**


*Chassis no. ZFFKW66A190168111. Bianco Avus with Italian flag stripe over black.* *Original, #2- condition.*


**Equipment:** 4308-cc/503-hp V-8, paddle-shift F1 six-speed, Scuderia shields, red calipers, Pirelli P Zero tires, carbon fiber interior trim.


**Condition:** One of 499 built. Showing 12,914 miles, it presents well with tiny chips on the front and light wear in the wheel wells. The headlights are both noticeably crazed across each lens, which stands out on a mostly clean car. Air intake metal at the top of the engine bay shows minor oxidation. Minor wear around the convertible top rubber. Lightly used and rare.


**Bottom line:** There is a lot of fanfare around modern Ferraris and the staggering prices they’ve fetched in 2026. The 16M is a perfect example. Basically an open version of the track-focused 430 Scuderia and built to celebrate Ferrari’s 16th Formula 1 Constructors’ World Championship, it’s never been a cheap car and has always been the priciest of the F430 family, but cheap can be a relative term. A year ago, these cars were selling for around half a million dollars. But starting in 2026, close to or more than $1M has been the new normal.


## Lot F19: 1977 Oldsmobile Cutlass NASCAR Stock Car


Mecum


**Sold for** **$99,000**


*Sold on bill of sale. Black and silver. Older restoration, #3 condition.*


**Equipment:** 355-cid/650-hp V-8, four-speed, side exhaust. Goodyear slicks, roll cage.


**Condition:** Driven by Buddy Baker to win the 1980 Daytona 500 from pole position at an average of 177.602 mph. Shown at the NASCAR Hall of Fame for two years. Restored in the mid-2000s, and the engine was refreshed in 2023. In used condition with the usual cracks and scratches you get with a race car. Dull finish on the wheels and some beat-up spots to the interior. Buddy Baker signed the dash. Great history for not a ton of money.


**Bottom line:** It’s hard not to think of this car as the best bargain of the week. Racing sports cars that never won anything sell for seven figures all the time in Monterey. In 2026, there were also two Indy 500-winning cars: Tony Kanaan’s 2013 car (a no-sale, asking[$800K](https://rmsothebys.com/auctions/mo26/lots/r0135-2013-dallara-dw12/) ), plus the 1931 Stevens-Miller “Bowes Seal Fast Special” (sold for[$1.6M](https://www.goodingco.com/lot/1931-stevens-miller-bowes-seal-fast-special) ). And here we have the car that took the checkered flag at one of America’s two most famous car races going for less than a new Escalade. There aren’t a ton of places to use old stock cars, but on history alone this was a serious deal.


## Lot F91: 1936 Mercedes-Benz 500K Roadster by Sindelfingen


Mecum


**Sold for** **$1,265,000**


*Chassis no. 130857. Red over tan leather. Older restoration, #2- condition.*


**Equipment:** RHD. 5018-cc/160-hp supercharged straight-eight, four-speed, chrome wire wheels with hub caps, single driving light, dual spotlight mirrors, top boot, dual rear-mounted spares, coach doors, VDO gauges.


**Condition:** Delivered new in London and in the U.S. by the mid-1950s. Represented with an early ’90s restoration. Represented as one of 29 Normal and Special Roadsters built on the 500K chassis, and one of five Normal Roadsters believed to still exist. Light pitting on some of the brightwork as well as mild age to the paint and interior. Tidy and clean underneath, aside from the older-looking exhaust. Not a show winner, but certainly attractive.


**Bottom line:** Prewar cars, at least the grander and more desirable ones, are still in demand even if the market for them isn’t as dynamic as other segments. This 500K, for example, sold here in 2022, in essentially the same condition, for essentially the same price: $1,270,000.


## Lot S115: 2011 Ferrari 599 GTO


Mecum


**Sold for** **$3,300,000**


*Chassis no. ZFF70RCA1B0177958. Blu Nart with Bianco Avus stripe over black cloth. Original, #2+ condition.*


**Equipment:** 5999-cc/661-hp V-12, F1 Superfast gearbox, telemetry kit, leather-wrapped roll bar, Brembo carbon ceramic disc brakes with silver aluminum calipers, Bose stereo, Racing Manettino, Virtual Racing Engineer.


**Condition:** Special-order Blu Nart with Bianco Avus livery, which reportedly cost over $17K. Showing 249 miles from new and no visible wear on the exterior or interior, this is a like-new car.


**Bottom line:** When Ferrari introduced the 599 GTO in 2010, it was claimed to be the company’s fastest-ever road car, lapping the Fiorano test circuit one second faster than the Enzo. Only 125 went to the U.S. market, out of a total production of 599 units. This is another price guide-breaking modern Ferrari, one that was typically a sub-million-dollar car 10 months ago. Then, there was a breakout sale in January as a car out of the now-famous Bachman Collection sold for a record[$3.96M](https://www.mecum.com/lots/1158452/2011-ferrari-599-gto/) . Since then, more have sold in the low-seven-figure range. This *Blu Nart* example is the second most expensive one we’ve seen, thanks to its unique colors and three-digit odometer reading.


## Lot S37: 1963 Chevrolet Corvette Z06


Mecum


**Sold for** **$770,000**


*Chassis no. 30837S108834. Sebring Silver over black vinyl. Older restoration, #1- condition.*


**Equipment:** 327-cid/360-hp L84 V-8, four-speed, N03 36-gallon fuel tank, power brakes, wheel covers, AM/FM radio, NCRS top flight, MCACN triple diamond.


**Condition:** The paint and brightwork are excellent, as is the panel fit; the engine compartment and underbody are like new, and the interior is like new. A beautiful “big tank” Z06 with an expert restoration and awards to prove it.


**Bottom line:** The Z06 option package added about $1800 to the cost of a new ’63 Corvette, which carried a base price of $4252. Just 199 examples sold, and just 63 of those got the large fuel tank that was offered with endurance racing in mind. Indeed, racing was the whole point of the Z06, which also added braking and handling upgrades on top of the L84 fuel-injected engine. Though it mostly failed in its on-track fight with Shelby’s new Cobra, the original Z06 has since become one of the most desirable Corvettes in the C2 (1963–67) family, and the large 36-gallon gas tank makes a six-figure difference in terms of value compared to a 20-gallon Z06.


This one was a $675K no-sale at Mecum Indy back in May of this year. The result here is healthier and more appropriate to the car’s impressive condition and equipment. Although Indy is a huge sale (Mecum’s second biggest, after Kissimmee), Monterey just has more deep pockets.


## Lot S105: 2003 Ferrari Enzo


Mecum


**Sold for** **$12,100,000**


*Chassis no. ZFFCW56A930134956. Rosso Corsa over Nero leather. Original, #2 condition.*


**Equipment:** 5999-cc/660-hp V-12, Scuderia shields, tool kit, factory cover, includes books and Ferrari Classiche service performed at the Ferrari factory.


**Condition:** One of 498 built. Just 589 original miles and in like-new condition on the outside. The driver’s seat leather has some stretching, but that’s it.


**Bottom line:** Yet another modern Ferrari that experienced a meteoric rise in value is the Enzo, the company’s halo model during the 2000s. This one is finished in a common color, though the mileage is low. It came to this same auction nine years ago, and it sold then for $2.97M. Even if you adjust that 2017 sale for inflation, the car still tripled in value. Three Enzos sold in Monterey this year, with this one coming in ahead of RM Sotheby’s 9800-mile car ([$9.41M](https://rmsothebys.com/auctions/mo26/lots/r0156-2003-ferrari-enzo/#/utm_source=rss&utm_medium=classified&utm_campaign=MO26) ) and Broad Arrow’s black, 13,200-mile example ([$10.675M](https://www.broadarrowauctions.com/vehicles/ql26_r0165/2003-ferrari-enzo) ). It is also the most expensive Rosso Corsa price ever recorded, 25% more than the next highest.


## Lot S74: 2005 Porsche Carrera GT


Mecum


**Sold for** **$3,575,000**


*Chassis no. WP0CA29805L001248. Rosso Fuoco over black leather. Visually maintained, largely original, #2 condition.*


**Equipment:** 5733-cc/605-hp V-10, six-speed manual, red calipers.


**Condition:** Refinished to PPG Rosso Fuoco from the original black. Showing 3480 believable miles. Excellent-quality paint and color change with no flaws visible. The rest of the car is in like-new condition. Driven sparingly and presents beautifully.


**Bottom line:** Barrett-Jackson sold this car in Scottsdale three years ago with 170 fewer miles on the odometer for $1,595,000. This car cost around 450 grand when it was new, but Carrera GTs have gained a lot of clout in recent years for being one of the last truly analog hypercars. Prices surged in the pandemic boom, then corrected down a bit in 2023–24, then shot up dramatically in 2026 as so many other modern exotics have. Though $3.575M isn’t a record, it’s still one of only a handful of Carrera GT transactions over $3M, and all of those have taken place in 2026.


## Lot S123: 1996 Ferrari F50


Mecum


**Sold for** **$14,575,000**


*Chassis no. ZFFTA46B000106690. Giallo Modena over black. Original, #2+ condition.*


**Equipment:** 4699-cc/513-hp V-12, six-speed, Scuderia shields, Ferrari driving shoes, three-piece Schedoni luggage set, tools and books.


**Condition:** The 239th of 349 F50s built and one of just 31 finished in this color. Ferrari Classiche certified. Delivered new to Switzerland. Looks almost too perfect for the 7248 km (4504 miles) showing. Recently serviced at Ferrari Lake Forest.


**Bottom line:** In early 2025, the world record auction price for a Ferrari F50 was $5.5M, and in 2010 an F50 wasn’t even worth $1M. Rarer than both its predecessor (F40) and its successor (Enzo), the F50 has seen a handful of eight-figure sales in 2026, and this is the highest. It beats by 19% the previous record set in January by the[Bachman Collection car](https://www.mecum.com/lots/1158440/1995-ferrari-f50/) . How much higher can these cars really go?


The post[9 Important Cars from the 2026 Mecum Monterey Auction](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/9-important-cars-from-the-2026-mecum-monterey-auction/) appeared first on[Hagerty Media](https://www.hagerty.com/media) .
